headline: Swiss startup ZuriQ and chipmaker Infineon expanded their partnership to build larger trapped-ion quantum chips.
score_reason: Pool score 5 lowered by one: the joint release is dated 7 Oct 2026; no timeline, money or size target is given.
importance_line: It pairs a quantum design with large-scale chip manufacturing, which could make quantum hardware easier to produce in Europe, but the work is at nine ions so far and the release gives no timeline or funding.
source: Infineon and ZuriQ (joint press release, via The Quantum Insider)
summary: Infineon, the German semiconductor maker, and ZuriQ, a quantum computing company spun out of ETH Zurich, announced in a joint press release carried by The Quantum Insider that they will extend their work on a chip design that holds ions in a flat two-dimensional grid. Earlier work trapped a 3-by-3 array of nine ions, which the companies call the largest two-dimensional array of its kind, and the next step is to scale to many more qubits.
notes: Original is the companies' joint press release; Data Center Dynamics page was blocked (403), so the link is the Quantum Insider page where the release text was read.
